api_doc_gaps.endpoint: ENT-FIN-004.docNo (DBF-FIN-035) — API-FIN-019/020/021, 'platform numbering engine'
api_doc_gaps.detail: CORE.md, srs-fin.md:118/123 and db-script-fin.md:55 all state docNo is generated by a 'platform numbering engine' scoped per fiscalYearId. No such component exists anywhere in this repo: no generator class in com.erp.common or any module, no number-series/sequence-config table in db/migration, and no existing entity with a system-generated business code. No later sub can invent one.
api_doc_gaps.resolution: HUMAN DECISION RECORDED (final, not to be relitigated). Format: docNo = JV-{fiscalYearCode}-{NNNNNN} — literal prefix 'JV-', then the owning fiscal year's code (FIN_FISCAL_YEAR.code, DBF-FIN-066, VARCHAR(10)), then '-', then a zero-padded 6-digit counter starting at 000001; worked example JV-2026-000123. Worst case length = 3 + 10 + 1 + 6 = 20 chars, comfortably inside doc_no VARCHAR(30). Counter scope and reset: scoped per fiscalYearId, restarting at 000001 for each new fiscal year, which aligns exactly with the existing UQ_FIN_JOURNAL_ENTRY_YEAR_DOCNO (fiscal_year_id, doc_no) constraint — the database therefore backs the uniqueness guarantee. The counter is NOT segmented by journalTypeCode: manual, event-built, recurring, allocation, reversal and the year-end CLOSING/OPENING entries all draw from one counter per fiscal year. Generator ownership: a FIN-local generator living in com.erp.fin, deliberately NOT a shared com.erp.common component — no other module needs document numbering today, so designing a general shared interface now would be speculative; it is promoted into common if and when a second real consumer appears. This is a conscious, recorded deviation from the ecosystem profile's standing guidance that numbering 'comes from the platform numbering engine; never generated in a module' — that guidance presumes an engine which does not exist in this repo, making literal compliance impossible. Immutability (unchanged): docNo is assigned once on create and never changes; excluded from every create and update request DTO, present only in responses. Implementation lands in the SVC-API phase, at journal-entry creation; the entity layer needs nothing beyond an immutable VARCHAR(30) column. Specs updated to match: CORE.md Numbering bullet, P3_1/backend-execution-plan-fin.md (Plan Index business-code row, entity registry row, CORE Numbering, DATA-DOM ENT-FIN-004 business code, SVC-API create orchestration) and packages/backend-execution/_SECTIONS.md.

api_doc_gaps.endpoint: Error Catalog row FIN-503 — any lookup-validating API (XM-FIN-001 unreachable)
api_doc_gaps.detail: The catalog declares a 503 outcome, but com.erp.common.domain.status.Status has no SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE constant (highest is INTERNAL_ERROR -> 500), so LocalizedException cannot express HTTP 503. Adding one would modify shared common infrastructure, which is outside FIN's scope.
api_doc_gaps.resolution: Resolved — the FIN-503 catalog row is unreachable and is struck; the Error Catalog goes from 32 rows to 31. Why: cross-module consumption in this repo is direct Spring interface injection within a single deployable, not loopback HTTP (see the javadoc on src/main/java/com/erp/mdl/crossmodule/MdlLookupApi.java, and the two delivered consumers NotificationLookupService and FileLookupService, which inject MdlLookupApi and call it in-process). With no network hop, 'MDL unreachable / 503' has no runtime producer. Corroborating: com.erp.common.domain.status.Status has no SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE constant (it tops out at INTERNAL_ERROR -> 500), GlobalExceptionHandler derives the HTTP status solely from Status, and gov-enforce-error-handling forbids a feature module modifying the shared enum — so 503 was unreachable by any sanctioned path regardless. Behaviour FIN adopts instead, following NotificationLookupService's delivered pattern: an invalid lookup code raises FIN-400-INVALID-LOOKUP; any other failure falls through to the existing, reachable FIN-500.

api_doc_gaps.endpoint: RULE-FIN-016 (lock an entry after posting) — every POSTED-entry mutation attempt; ENT-FIN-004.statusCode
api_doc_gaps.detail: The Error Catalog in packages/backend-execution/_SECTIONS.md registers no code for RULE-FIN-016; its own RULE->code coverage line says '(enforced by omission, no code needed — no UPDATE/DELETE mapping exists on a POSTED row)'. srs-fin.md §A5 nevertheless gives the rule a bilingual message ('القيد المُرحَّل مقفل؛ التصحيح فقط عبر العكس' / 'A posted entry is locked; correction is only through a reversal'), and CORE.md mandates a domain guard for every rule answering 'is this operation allowed?' — so JournalEntryDomain.assertNotPosted() needs a registered code to throw and the catalog supplies none. Inventing one is forbidden by the contract ground-truth rule.
api_doc_gaps.resolution: RESOLVED — not deferred, and there is no spec gap to clarify. The positive guard JournalEntryDomain.assertNotPosted() has been removed as a latent bug: it would have rejected every legal reversal. FIN's API registry declares no PUT and no DELETE on /journal-entries, so the only code path that ever writes an already-POSTED row is the reversal flow (API-FIN-021), and that write is deliberate — SVC-API-INT.md specifies setting originalEntryId/reversalEntryId on both rows, SRS A7's state machine defines POSTED --(reverse action)--> VOID for the original, and JournalEntry.voidByReversal(...) performs exactly that. The guard's own javadoc told the service to call it 'before any mutation of an existing entry'; wired as instructed it would have thrown on every reversal. RULE-FIN-016's own SRS text carves this out ('reject any edit or delete attempt... correction is only through a reversal'), so reversal is the rule's exception, not its target. Left uncalled instead it would be dead code, which gov-validate-backend-feature and contract rule A.2.9 both flag. RULE-FIN-016 is therefore enforced by omission exactly as the execution plan already states ('enforced by omission, no code needed — no UPDATE/DELETE mapping exists on a POSTED row'): JournalEntryRepository declares no @Modifying query and no derived deleteBy..., which is the enforcement mechanism and stays untouched. Precedent: MDL's RULE-MDL-003 (key immutability) — owned by LookupTypeDomain for traceability, carrying its SRS message, enforced purely structurally, with no guard method and no error code, and independently verified compliant. JournalEntryDomain's class javadoc now documents the rule the same way, including the reversal carve-out. FIN-409-INVALID-TRANSITION stays in FinErrorCodes and in both message bundles as the period soft-close row it actually is; its javadoc no longer claims to cover POSTED-entry mutation. No new error-code row should ever be requested for RULE-FIN-016.

api_doc_gaps.endpoint: POST /api/v1/fin/accounts (API-FIN-002) — parentAccountId handling, RULE-FIN-001 create trigger
api_doc_gaps.detail: API-FIN-002's Orchestration line and its Errors line specify mutually exclusive behaviours for the same input. Orchestration says: 'if parentAccountId given, flip the parent's isLeafFl to false via RULE-FIN-001's inverse effect (a parent gaining its first child can no longer itself be a leaf)'. Errors lists FIN-409-PARENT-NOT-LEAF-ELIGIBLE, and the delivered DATA-DOM-MASTER domain guard AccountDomain.create(code, leaf, parentIsLeaf) throws exactly that code when the chosen parent is still marked leaf, with javadoc stating 'the parent must be demoted first (Account.markAsParent())'. Auto-flipping would make the guard unreachable and FIN-409-PARENT-NOT-LEAF-ELIGIBLE dead in both the code table and both message bundles; rejecting means no flip ever happens.
api_doc_gaps.resolution: Implemented in favour of the delivered domain guard: AccountService.create resolves the parent, then calls AccountDomain.create(...), which rejects a parent still marked as accepting direct posting with FIN-409-PARENT-NOT-LEAF-ELIGIBLE. No code change was needed for this resolution — the delivered behaviour already matches it (verified against AccountService.create and AccountDomain.create). Grounding (strengthened; the earlier 'DATA-DOM is COMPLETE' argument was the weakest of the available ones and is no longer the basis): (1) RULE-FIN-001's own scope in srs-fin.md §A5 states 'Trigger: on update (isLeafFl)' — the rule is triggered by an attempt to change isLeafFl, and it never authorises the system to flip a parent's flag by itself on a child-create; (2) AC-FIN-002 says 'Then the system rejects the change', which is rejection, not silent mutation; (3) the API-FIN-002 block's own Validations line already says the check targets the parent and expects rejection — 'at create this only matters when the same call sets a parent that itself must remain non-leaf — QR-FIN-006 checks the *parent*, not the new row'; (4) under the auto-flip reading the catalogued code FIN-409-PARENT-NOT-LEAF-ELIGIBLE would have no trigger anywhere in the system — it is catalogued against API-FIN-002 only, so auto-flipping would leave it dead in FinErrorCodes and in both message bundles. The erroneous line is therefore the block's Orchestration sentence ('if parentAccountId given, flip the parent's isLeafFl to false via RULE-FIN-001's inverse effect'), which contradicts the same block's Validations and Errors lines as well as the SRS rule and its AC. Demotion of a parent remains available explicitly through API-FIN-003. No spec file was edited.

api_doc_gaps.endpoint: POST /api/v1/fin/journal-entries (API-FIN-019) — 'every failure returned together (REQ-FIN-015)'
api_doc_gaps.detail: API-FIN-019's Validations line requires RULE-FIN-006/007/008/009 failures to be 'returned together', but the shared error envelope cannot express that: com.erp.common.exception.LocalizedException carries exactly one Status and one errorCode, GlobalExceptionHandler renders it as a single ApiError, and the multi-item FieldErrorItem list is populated only by bean-validation (MethodArgumentNotValidException). The four delivered domain guards (JournalEntryDomain.assertBalanced/assertTargetPeriodOpen, AccountDomain.assertPostable, DimensionValueDomain.assertUsableOnLine) each throw on first violation by construction. Aggregating them would require either modifying shared common infrastructure (forbidden) or reimplementing the rules outside the domain classes (A.5.18 automatic rejection).
api_doc_gaps.resolution: RESOLVED — implemented, not deferred. The requirement was real and the delivered fail-fast behaviour did violate AC-FIN-015 ('Given a manual entry with two failing validations ... Then the system returns both failures and posts nothing'). A human explicitly approved an additive change to com.erp.common to close it; that approval is the sole basis for touching shared infrastructure and its scope is exactly what is listed here. Shape implemented: (1) new record com.erp.common.exception.ErrorDetail(String errorCode, Object... args) — one failure carrying exactly what a single-code LocalizedException carries, so each entry localizes through the existing MessageSource lookup identically; (2) a second LocalizedException constructor (Status, List<ErrorDetail>) alongside the untouched (Status, String, Object...) one — the first detail supplies the existing top-level errorCode/args, the whole list is kept in a new transient List<ErrorDetail> errors that is List.of() for every single-code throw; (3) GlobalExceptionHandler.handleLocalizedException now also fills the fieldErrors list ApiError already exposed — one FieldErrorItem per failure (field = error code, message = the resolved bundle message) — only when errors is non-empty. Status enum, the Status->HTTP mapping and ApiError's fields are unchanged, so a single-code throw serializes byte-identically to before and all 140 existing LocalizedException call sites across sec/mdl/cu/notif/file/fin compile and behave unchanged. Domain layer: each guard gained a NON-THROWING sibling returning Optional<ErrorDetail> — JournalEntryDomain.checkBalanced / checkTargetPeriodOpen, AccountDomain.checkPostable, DimensionValueDomain.checkUsableOnLine — and the existing assertBalanced / assertTargetPeriodOpen / assertPostable / assertUsableOnLine now delegate to them, so every rule keeps ONE implementation and the throwing API is unchanged for every other caller (event build, recurring, allocation, reversal). JournalEntryService.createManual evaluates every applicable guard through the check* siblings, collects the returned ErrorDetails and throws ONCE with Status.CONFLICT and the full list (all four codes are 409, so the HTTP status is unchanged); the service contains no business condition of its own, so A.5.18 still holds. Not-found preconditions (year, period, account, dimension, dimension value) and XM-FIN-001 lookup validation deliberately stay fail-fast: an unresolvable reference leaves nothing to validate. Atomicity is untouched — the aggregate is still assembled in memory, the aggregate throw happens before JournalEntry.post(...) and before the single repository.save(...), inside the one @Transactional method. Verified: mvn compile and the full mvn test suite (8 tests, incl. CrossModuleBoundaryArchTest) pass on JDK 25.

api_doc_gaps.endpoint: POST /api/v1/fin/journal-entries/from-event (API-FIN-020) — request body shape, and ACCOUNT_DERIVATION_TYPE=MAPPING
api_doc_gaps.detail: API-FIN-020's Request line is 'the canonical accounting event payload (opaque shape, out-of-scope Event consumer, POL-FIN-020)' — no field list exists anywhere in P1/P2/P3_1, yet the rule engine must read named fields off it: a RuleLine with accountDerivationTypeCode=DIRECT names an event field holding an account code (DBF-FIN-102), and one with amountSourceTypeCode=FIELD names an event amount field (DBF-FIN-104). Separately, accountDerivationTypeCode=MAPPING implies a mapping store that db-script-fin.md declares nowhere: ENT-FIN-010 carries only the type/value pair and there is no mapping table among the 14 FIN tables.
api_doc_gaps.resolution: HUMAN DECISION APPLIED (final). (a) MAPPING now FAILS LOUDLY instead of being collapsed into DIRECT. srs-fin.md ENT-FIN-010 defines accountDerivationValue as 'constant account code, event field name, or mapping-set key' — one meaning per ACCOUNT_DERIVATION_TYPE — and no mapping store exists in db-script-fin.md's 14 tables, so reading a mapping-set key as an event field name silently resolved a line to the wrong account or to none: the one outcome a ledger must never produce. A new Error Catalog row FIN-422-MAPPING-UNSUPPORTED (PLATFORM-STD, API-FIN-020, HTTP 422, ar: 'يستخدم هذا السطر اشتقاق الحساب عبر جدول المطابقة وهو غير متاح حاليًا' / en: 'This rule line uses mapping-based account derivation, which is not available yet') was added to _SECTIONS.md and the plan's copy, registered as FinErrorCodes.FIN_422_MAPPING_UNSUPPORTED and added to BOTH message bundles. HTTP 422 / Status.BUSINESS_RULE_VIOLATION was chosen because the request is structurally valid (not 400) and nothing is missing on the wire (not 404) and no record blocks it (not 409): a stored configuration cannot be executed, which is exactly the taxonomy's 'invariant violation that is not about a specific referencing record'. 501 was unavailable — Status declares no NOT_IMPLEMENTED and a feature module may not extend the shared enum (the same constraint that struck FIN-503). EventTypeRuleDomain.resolveAccountCode now branches explicitly: CONSTANT returns the value as the account code, MAPPING throws the new code, anything else (DIRECT) reads the named event field — the MAPPING fall-through into the DIRECT branch is gone. CONSTANT and DIRECT keep working unchanged. (b) The request-shape half of this gap is UNCHANGED and still open: EventEntryBuildRequest keeps the narrowest shape that invents nothing ({eventReference, eventTypeCode, docDate, baseAmount, amounts, fields, descriptionAr, descriptionEn}) pending the Event consumer's real contract.

api_doc_gaps.endpoint: POST /api/v1/fin/fiscal-years (API-FIN-023) — generated periods' NAME_AR / NAME_EN and their date spans
api_doc_gaps.detail: API-FIN-023's Request is {code, startDate, endDate, periodCount} and its Orchestration says 'generate periodCount periods, each statusCode=OPEN'. FIN_FISCAL_PERIOD.NAME_AR and NAME_EN are NOT NULL (DBF-FIN-078/079, db-script-fin.md §3 BLOCK 3, V22__fin_schema.sql) and START_DATE/END_DATE are NOT NULL too (DBF-FIN-080/081), but nothing in the SRS, db-script or execution plan says what a generated period is named or how the year's span is divided.
api_doc_gaps.resolution: HUMAN DECISION APPLIED (final) — periods are calendar months when there are twelve. The previous even split of DAYS produced 31/31/31/30… blocks whose boundaries drifted off month ends, so entries landed in the wrong period and every period-scoped report was wrong. Rule now governed, not implicit: SVC-API-INT.md's API-FIN-023 block (and the plan's copy) states it — when periodCount = 12 and [startDate, endDate] covers one whole year starting on the first of a month, period N IS the Nth calendar month of the span (1st to last day) and its NAME_AR/NAME_EN are that month's own name in Arabic and English; for any other period count, or a span that is not a whole year, the even day split remains the fallback, with the first (totalDays mod periodCount) blocks one day longer and 'الفترة N' / 'Period N' names. Implemented in FiscalPeriodDomain.generatedPeriod(yearStart, yearEnd, periodNo, periodCount), returning a GeneratedPeriod(startDate, endDate, nameAr, nameEn) record; FiscalYearMapper.toPeriodEntity now only builds the row from it. Month names come from the platform's own locale data — java.time.Month.getDisplayName(TextStyle.FULL, locale) over the JDK's CLDR data, for Locale 'ar' and Locale.ENGLISH — not a hardcoded Arabic string table. The project's MessageSource bundles were NOT used for them: those bundles are the error-code/validation-key register (keys are wire codes) and the codebase exposes no localization mechanism for persisted row content; CLDR is the standard source for calendar names and needs no per-deployment upkeep. Only the fallback labels 'الفترة '/'Period ' remain as literals, since a non-calendar block has no name in any locale data.

api_doc_gaps.endpoint: POST /api/v1/fin/fiscal-years/{id}/year-end-close (API-FIN-027) — Retained Earnings account, next fiscal year, and RULE-FIN-008 on the closing entry
api_doc_gaps.detail: Three problems in one block. (1) The Orchestration line says 'result accounts -> Retained Earnings' but FIN_ACCOUNT carries no retained-earnings marker (DBF-FIN-001..013) and ACCOUNT_TYPE only reaches EQUITY, which many accounts can share — the account cannot be derived. (2) It says 'build + post the next year's opening entry' but FIN_FISCAL_YEAR declares no successor link (DBF-FIN-065..074); inferring one from adjacent dates would invent a rule. (3) CONTRADICTION: the API's own Validations line requires every period of the year to be HARD_CLOSE before the close runs, while its Repository line routes BOTH generated entries through QR-FIN-029..033 — which includes QR-FIN-031, RULE-FIN-008's 'the entry's period is Open at post time'. Under that reading the closing entry can never post, because no Open period exists in the year by construction.
api_doc_gaps.resolution: HUMAN DECISION APPLIED (final) — all three parts; the invented YearEndCloseRequest is DELETED and API-FIN-027's request is the path id again, exactly as the plan states. (1) RETAINED EARNINGS gets a real marker. New forward migration V23__fin_account_retained_earnings_flag.sql (V22 untouched) adds FIN_ACCOUNT.is_retained_earnings_fl BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE and guarantees AT MOST ONE marked account through the partial unique index UQ_FIN_ACCOUNT_RETAINED_EARNINGS ON FIN_ACCOUNT (is_retained_earnings_fl) WHERE is_retained_earnings_fl — partial, because a plain UNIQUE over the column would also cap the number of FALSE rows at one; Postgres has no partial UNIQUE *constraint*, hence CREATE UNIQUE INDEX. Registered as DBF-FIN-147 in db-script-fin.md's FIN_ACCOUNT matrix, CREATE TABLE, COMMENT and index blocks, in the DB Alignment Manifest in both _SECTIONS.md and P3_1 (counts 146 -> 147), and in P2/registry-db-fin.md. Account gains the mapped field (native BOOLEAN, no converter per A.1.6; the partial index is documented on the field rather than mis-declared as a total @UniqueConstraint), AccountResponse and AccountMapper expose it READ-ONLY, and it is deliberately NOT settable through API-FIN-002/003: SVC-API-CRUD.md fixes those request contracts field by field and neither lists it, and a caller-settable marker would reinstate exactly the unaudited ledger decision this replaces; it is set as data, and a governed endpoint would need a new API id. FiscalYearService.retainedEarningsAccount() derives it via AccountRepository.findFirstByIsRetainedEarningsFlTrueOrderByAccountPkAsc(); none marked raises the existing FIN-404-ACCOUNT (no new code invented), and a second marked account is unreachable behind the index. (2) RULE-FIN-008's exemption is now part of the RULE. srs-fin.md §A5 RULE-FIN-008's Statement was amended (the single sanctioned edit to that file) to exempt the year-end closing and opening entries, noting the exemption applies to no other entry and to no other rule; the wording was propagated to the DATA-DOM ENT-FIN-008 block (DATA-DOM-MASTER.md), DATA-DOM-TRANSACTIONAL.md, SVC-API-INT.md and both the _SECTIONS.md and P3_1 copies (including the QR-FIN-031 registry row). API-FIN-027's Repository line — the genuinely imprecise line — now reads QR-FIN-041, QR-FIN-029, QR-FIN-030, QR-FIN-032, QR-FIN-033 and states that QR-FIN-031 is not applied to either generated entry. In code the parameterised hole is GONE: JournalPostingService.PostingRequest.periodGateApplies is deleted (zero occurrences in src/) and the exemption lives in the domain layer as JournalEntryDomain.checkTargetPeriodOpenForGeneratedEntry(journalTypeCode, statusCode), which decides from what the entry IS (isYearEndGenerated: JOURNAL_TYPE CLOSING/OPENING, constants moved onto JournalEntryDomain and re-exported by JournalPostingService) and otherwise delegates to the unchanged single implementation checkTargetPeriodOpen(statusCode). API-FIN-019's manual path keeps the unconditional form on purpose, so a caller-supplied journalTypeCode can never buy the exemption. RULE-FIN-006/007/009 still apply to both generated entries in full. The closing entry posts into the year's LAST period, as before. (3) SUCCESSOR YEAR — DERIVED DECISION, MADE IN THE ABSENCE OF AN ARTIFACT, OPEN TO BEING OVERRULED: no spec states how the next fiscal year is found and FIN_FISCAL_YEAR declares no successor column (DBF-FIN-065..074), so the only derivation the schema supports was taken — ADJACENCY: the fiscal year whose startDate is the day after this year's endDate (FiscalYearRepository.findByStartDate, FiscalYearService.successorOf). No such year raises the existing FIN-404-YEAR rather than guessing. This is NOT something the specs stated; it is recorded in SVC-API-INT.md's API-FIN-027 Repository line as DERIVED and should be replaced by an explicit successor link or a stated rule if a human decides otherwise.

api_doc_gaps.endpoint: POST /api/v1/fin/recurring-templates/{id}/run (API-FIN-014) — no not-found error code for a RecurringTemplate
api_doc_gaps.detail: API-FIN-014 loads the template by id (QR-FIN-019) and its Errors line says only 'same as API-FIN-019', whose codes are the four post-time rule codes plus FIN-404-YEAR / FIN-404-PERIOD / FIN-404-ACCOUNT. The Error Catalog in _SECTIONS.md carries no FIN-404-TEMPLATE row (nor any other row for ENT-FIN-011), so an unknown template id has no registered code to raise, and inventing one is forbidden by the contract ground-truth rule.
api_doc_gaps.resolution: HUMAN DECISION APPLIED (final) — FIN-404-TEMPLATE now exists. The catalog assigns a distinct 404 per entity (ACCOUNT, DIMENSION, RULE, ALLOCATION-RULE, ENTRY, PERIOD, YEAR) and had no row for ENT-FIN-011, so an unknown recurring template id was reported as FIN-404-RULE ('Rule not found'), naming the wrong entity to the client. A new row in the same uniform style — | FIN-404-TEMPLATE | PLATFORM-STD | API-FIN-014 | 404 | unknown recurring template id | القالب المتكرر غير موجود | Recurring template not found | — was added to the Error Catalog in _SECTIONS.md and the plan's copy, registered as FinErrorCodes.FIN_404_TEMPLATE with Status.NOT_FOUND, added to both message bundles, and is now raised by the one orElseThrow in RecurringTemplateService.run. API-FIN-014's Errors line reads 'same as API-FIN-019, plus FIN-404-TEMPLATE'. FIN-404-RULE stays exactly where it belongs, on the event-type rule (RuleLineService).

api_doc_gaps.endpoint: GET /api/v1/fin/reports/income-statement (API-FIN-031) — the 'period range' request parameter
api_doc_gaps.detail: API-FIN-031's Request line is 'fiscalYearId(EXACT), period range'. 'period range' names no field anywhere: srs-fin.md REQ-FIN-042 / AC-FIN-042 and its A8 screen table say only 'fiscalYearId, period range', db-script-fin.md defines no range column, and the plan's API registry, QRC (QR-FIN-043) and DB Alignment Manifest carry nothing either. Neither the parameter names nor their type (period ids? period numbers? dates?) are stated, so the shape had to be chosen rather than read. Separately, the block's Errors line names only FIN-500, which leaves an unresolvable range bound with no stated outcome.
api_doc_gaps.resolution: RESOLVED at the DOC phase — no longer blocked, and no spec clarification is needed. What the spec left unstated was the PARAMETER NAMES, not the semantics: 'period range' has exactly one meaning the delivered artifacts can support, and the implementation took it without inventing anything. Verified at DOC against all three grounds. (1) SCHEMA — the range needs no new column or concept: FIN_FISCAL_PERIOD already carries fiscal_period_pk (DBF-FIN-075) plus start_date (DBF-FIN-080) and end_date (DBF-FIN-081), all NOT NULL, in db-script-fin.md §1/§3 and in V22; a range of periods therefore already IS a range of dates, derivable from rows that exist. (2) SIBLING PRECEDENT — the other reports scope identically. ReportService.trialBalance (API-FIN-029), balanceSheet (API-FIN-030) and incomeStatement (API-FIN-031) all narrow through the SAME shared QR-FIN-043 aggregation, the single private ReportService.balanceRows(periodId, fiscalYearId, fromDate, toDate, accountTypeCodes) call onto JournalLineRepository.aggregateAccountBalances(...); balanceSheet already passes a docDate bound (asOfDate) into that same toDate parameter, so the income statement translating its two period ids into the fromDate/toDate bounds of that identical signature is the established pattern, not a new mechanism. (3) NO INVENTED ERROR CODE — an unresolvable period id raises the ALREADY REGISTERED FIN-404-PERIOD (FinErrorCodes.FIN_404_PERIOD, Status.NOT_FOUND, present in both i18n bundles: messages.properties 'Period not found' / messages_ar.properties 'الفترة غير موجودة') from ReportService.periodOf; no catalog row was added and API-FIN-031's Errors line (FIN-500) is untouched. DELIVERED SHAPE, unchanged by this resolution: two OPTIONAL query parameters fromPeriodId and toPeriodId on GET /api/v1/fin/reports/income-statement, translated to fromPeriodId -> its startDate and toPeriodId -> its endDate; both omitted means the whole fiscal year, which is REQ-FIN-042's own scope; the applied range is echoed back in IncomeStatementResponse.fromPeriodId/toPeriodId/fromDate/toDate so the client sees exactly what was used. The names fromPeriodId/toPeriodId are recorded as a NAMING CONVENTION chosen for consistency with the module's existing periodId/fiscalYearId/asOfDate report parameters — a convention, not an invented contract term; a human may rename them without any semantic consequence.

api_doc_gaps.endpoint: XM-FIN-001 — keys FISCAL_YEAR_STATUS (DBF-FIN-069), PERIOD_STATE (DBF-FIN-082), JOURNAL_STATUS (DBF-FIN-040)
api_doc_gaps.detail: INT-C.md states FIN calls MdlLookupApi.readActiveValuesByKey(typeKey) 'for every one of FIN's 13 owned keys, at the point each lookup-backed field is written'. Nine keys have a real call site (ACCOUNT_TYPE, DEBIT_CREDIT, JOURNAL_TYPE, ACCOUNTING_EVENT_TYPE, ACCOUNT_DERIVATION_TYPE, AMOUNT_SOURCE_TYPE, DISTRIBUTION_TYPE, RECURRING_SCHEDULE_TYPE, RECURRING_FREQUENCY); PAYMENT_METHOD legitimately has none (P1/registry-srs-fin.md:42 — 'registered, no dedicated column this v1'). The remaining three are the state/status columns: they are excluded from every request DTO (system-assigned, see FiscalYearCreateRequest and JournalEntryCreateRequest javadoc) and are written by FIN from hardcoded String literals in the domain/service layer (11 occurrences of 'DRAFT'/'POSTED'/'VOID'/'OPEN'/'CLOSED'/'HARD_CLOSE'/'YEAR_END_CLOSE' under src/main/java/com/erp/fin), never checked against MDL. No client-writable lookup-backed column is unvalidated, so this is not an exploitable hole today, but the literals FIN writes are not guaranteed to be active values of their MDL type: if MDL's FISCAL_YEAR_STATUS/PERIOD_STATE/JOURNAL_STATUS seed drifts or a value is deactivated, FIN silently persists a code MDL no longer recognises and no test detects it.
api_doc_gaps.resolution: RESOLVED (INT-R) — NOT a gap; XM-FIN-001 governs client-submitted codes only, and these three are system-assigned state. Grounds: (1) INT-C.md's XM-FIN-001 Contract reads 'data required = the submitted code exists as an active value under the named type ... fallback if absent = reject with FIN-400-INVALID-LOOKUP', and its Interface line triggers 'at the point each lookup-backed field is written or offered as a select-list'. A 'reject the submitted code' fallback is incoherent for a value no client submits: FIN cannot answer its own state transition with a 400 client-validation error. (2) Client-reachability re-checked in code at INT-R: there is no setStatusCode anywhere under src/main/java/com/erp/fin, no request DTO carries statusCode (FiscalYearCreateRequest:16, JournalEntryCreateRequest:19 and EventEntryBuildRequest:39 all list it among the excluded system-assigned fields; JournalEntryService:149 states 'statusCode is system-assigned and never submitted'), and every write is an entity-owned transition from a compile-time constant (JournalEntry.STATUS_DRAFT/POSTED/VOID at JournalEntry.java:95-101,150,212,222; FiscalYear.STATUS_OPEN/CLOSED at FiscalYear.java:59-62,96,124; FiscalPeriod.STATUS_OPEN/SOFT_CLOSE/HARD_CLOSE/YEAR_END_CLOSE at FiscalPeriod.java:64-73,119). The only client-facing exposure is JournalEntrySearchRequest's statusCode EXACT filter — a read predicate, not a write, and an unknown value there returns an empty page, not a bad write. (3) SRS A7 (srs-fin.md:1067-1090) models all three as state machines whose transitions are driven by REQ-FIN-017/028/032/033/034/036 — system actions — and A6/registry-srs-fin.md frame these keys as FIN-owned value lists backing those states, not as client input. Conclusion: the nine client-submitted keys are validated, PAYMENT_METHOD has no column this v1, and these three are out of XM-FIN-001's scope. No per-write validation is added. RESIDUAL RISK (carried forward, unchanged from the INT-C finding): FIN writes these literals unconditionally, so if MDL's FISCAL_YEAR_STATUS / PERIOD_STATE / JOURNAL_STATUS seed drifts or a value is deactivated, FIN keeps persisting a code MDL no longer recognises and nothing fails loudly. That is a seed-consistency concern between FIN's entity constants and MDL's seed data — to be handled by a later phase (ALIGN-BE / seed reconciliation), not by a per-write lookup call.

api_doc_gaps.endpoint: POST /api/v1/fin/journal-entries/{id}/reverse (API-FIN-021) and every reversing recurring template run (API-FIN-014) — RULE-FIN-011/013, ACCOUNTING §12 points 7 and 9
api_doc_gaps.detail: LEDGER-BREAKING. The reversal flow does BOTH halves of two mutually exclusive designs: JournalEntryService.reverse (:254-263) posts the mirrored entry (JournalPostingService:159 leaves it POSTED) AND sets the original to VOID (JournalEntry.voidByReversal, entity/JournalEntry.java:220-223). Every balance read filters statusCode = POSTED only (JournalLineRepository:111 aggregateAccountBalances, :70 ledger; JournalLineDimensionRepository dimension aggregate; AllocationRuleService:260-262; FiscalYearService:270-272), so the original's lines vanish from every report while the mirror remains. Net ledger effect of a reversal is MINUS the original, not zero. Reproduce: post DR Cash 1000 / CR Revenue 1000, then reverse it; the trial balance afterwards shows Cash CR 1000 and Revenue DR 1000 — an invented, inverted transaction. It still balances, so the §12 point-8 'balances by construction' check does not catch it. RecurringTemplateService:250-258 has the same shape, so a REVERSING template's only ledger footprint is the inverse of its accrual. ReportService:44-45 documents the intended semantics ('a VOID one drops out of it the moment its reversal posts') which is correct ONLY if the mirror is not posted.
api_doc_gaps.resolution: RESOLVED — HUMAN DECISION: option (a) CLASSIC REVERSAL, applied in code and specs. The original entry now STAYS POSTED for good; the mirror reversal is posted alongside it and the two rows stay linked in both directions (originalEntryId / reversalEntryId, DBF-FIN-042/043). Implemented: JournalEntry.voidByReversal(JournalEntry) was reduced to a pure link-setter and renamed JournalEntry.linkReversal(JournalEntry) — it now assigns only reversalEntry and no longer writes statusCode; both call sites were updated (JournalEntryService.reverse, API-FIN-021, and RecurringTemplateService.postReversalInNextPeriod, API-FIN-014 — the second site had the identical defect and is fixed by the same change). No guard changed: RULE-FIN-013 (JournalEntryDomain.assertCanReverse, FIN-409-NOT-POSTED), RULE-FIN-011's mirroring and RULE-FIN-012's period substitution are untouched. Net ledger effect of a reversal is now exactly zero: both entries are POSTED, so both are seen by the POSTED-only reads (JournalLineRepository.aggregateAccountBalances and findAccountLedgerLines, the dimension aggregate, AllocationRuleService and FiscalYearService), and each reversal line carries the opposite directionCode of its original, so the debit and credit sums cancel per account. Side effect, deliberate: RULE-FIN-016 (a POSTED row is never modified) now holds with NO carve-out at all — the only write back to the original is the reversalEntryId link, never its accounting state; the 'sanctioned carve-out' language was removed from JournalEntry, JournalEntryDomain, JournalEntryService and RecurringTemplateService. Specs amended: srs-fin.md §A7 state machine (POSTED is now terminal; the reverse action performs no transition), packages/backend-execution/DATA-DOM/DATA-DOM-TRANSACTIONAL.md and SVC-API/SVC-API-INT.md, and the P3_1/backend-execution-plan-fin.md plan copy of both. Test expectations updated (ids and TC markers unchanged): TC-FIN-028 now asserts the original stays POSTED and that the pair nets to zero, TC-FIN-024 asserts the period-N accrual stays POSTED, TC-FIN-030's precondition became a DRAFT entry. JournalEntry.STATUS_VOID and the JOURNAL_STATUS lookup value 'VOID' now have NO writer anywhere in FIN; both were deliberately RETAINED and nothing was removed from any spec — JOURNAL_STATUS is shared MDL lookup data (XM-FIN-001) and retiring a lookup value is a separate, explicit decision. FOLLOW-UP NOW CLOSED (double-reversal hole): because a reversed entry stays POSTED, RULE-FIN-013's status half stopped catching a second reverse of the same entry, which would have posted a second mirror and left a net ledger effect of -(original). AC-FIN-030 always required that rejection, so no new rule was invented — only the code for an already-stated requirement. Guard: JournalEntryDomain.assertCanReverse() became assertCanReverse(boolean alreadyReversed) — RULE-FIN-013 keeps exactly ONE implementation, now carrying both halves (non-POSTED -> FIN-409-NOT-POSTED; already linked -> FIN-409-ALREADY-REVERSED). The fact is resolved by the service from the loaded row's REVERSAL_ENTRY_ID (DBF-FIN-043) and passed in as a plain argument, so the domain class still touches no repository (A.0.3) and no business-rule if is inlined in a service (A.5.18). Applied to BOTH reversal paths: JournalEntryService.reverse (API-FIN-021) and RecurringTemplateService.postReversalInNextPeriod (API-FIN-014) — the two and only two linkReversal call sites. New Error Catalog row FIN-409-ALREADY-REVERSED | RULE-FIN-013 | API-FIN-021, 014 | 409, added to packages/backend-execution/_SECTIONS.md and the P3_1/backend-execution-plan-fin.md copy; 409/Status.CONFLICT rather than 422 because the block comes from the existence of a specific referencing record (the reversal entry already pointing at this one), which is the taxonomy's CONFLICT row. Constant appended to FinErrorCodes and the message added to both i18n bundles (32 FIN keys each, parity kept). SRS amended (narrow correction of the two lines the classic-reversal decision made untrue): srs-fin.md line 682 rationale now reads 'prevents double-reversal (an entry that already carries a reversal link) or reversing a DRAFT row', and AC-FIN-030's Given at line 686 now reads 'an entry already reversed once (it stays POSTED and carries a reversalEntryId link to its reversal)'. The same claim was corrected in DATA-DOM/DATA-DOM-TRANSACTIONAL.md, SVC-API/SVC-API-INT.md (Validations/Errors/Orchestration), the QR-FIN-035 and RULE-to-code coverage lines in _SECTIONS.md, the P3_1 plan copy of all of the above, and test_gen/test-execution-manifest-fin.md's CRUD matrix ('VOID via reverse' -> no VOID path). Test coverage restored as a linked-entry precondition instead of a VOID one: NEW TC-FIN-048 (RULE-FIN-013 -> FIN-409-ALREADY-REVERSED) in packages/backend-test/RULE-SCENARIOS.md and test_gen/backend-test-plan-fin.md, registered in the traceability index, the coverage note, backend-test/state.json markers and the test-execution manifest; TC-FIN-030 keeps its id, marker and DRAFT precondition and now points at TC-FIN-048. api_doc_gaps.endpoint: XM-FIN-001 — all 13 FIN-owned MDL lookup types; blocks API-FIN-002/006/007/010/011/013/016/019/020 on a fresh deployment
api_doc_gaps.detail: No migration seeds ANY FIN lookup type or value into MDL_LOOKUP_TYPE / MDL_LOOKUP_VALUE. The only INSERTs into MDL_LOOKUP_TYPE in the whole repo are V20__notif_file_lookup_data_migration.sql:66-78, which seeds NOTIF/FILE types only. MdlLookupApiImpl.readActiveValuesByKey (crossmodule/MdlLookupApiImpl.java:53-58) throws MDL-404-TYPE-KEY when the key is absent or inactive; FinLookupValidationService.assertValidCode (:114-125) relabels exactly that to FIN-400-INVALID-LOOKUP with Status.VALIDATION_ERROR. Consequence on a fresh database: POST /api/v1/fin/accounts fails with HTTP 400 / FIN-400-INVALID-LOOKUP on accountTypeCode before any account can exist, and the same holds for every create that carries a lookup-backed column (ACCOUNT_TYPE, DEBIT_CREDIT, JOURNAL_TYPE, ACCOUNTING_EVENT_TYPE, ACCOUNT_DERIVATION_TYPE, AMOUNT_SOURCE_TYPE, DISTRIBUTION_TYPE, RECURRING_SCHEDULE_TYPE, RECURRING_FREQUENCY). FIN is therefore entirely unusable out of the box — a strictly larger blocker than the two already recorded, and it was never noticed because INT-C/INT-R only verified the CALL, never that the data it reads exists.
api_doc_gaps.resolution: HUMAN DECISION APPLIED (final) — shape (a): FIN authors its own forward migration seeding MDL's tables, mirroring the precedent V20 set (NOTIF/FILE seed their own lookup types straight into MDL_LOOKUP_TYPE/MDL_LOOKUP_VALUE) and the one V24 set (FIN seeds its own screens straight into SEC's registry tables). Shape (b) is rejected: an undocumented manual onboarding step would leave every fresh deployment and every backend test run broken until someone remembered it. Delivered as src/main/resources/db/migration/V26__fin_mdl_lookup_seed.sql — 13 MDL_LOOKUP_TYPE rows, all OWNER_MODULE_CODE='FIN', plus 36 MDL_LOOKUP_VALUE rows, all active, PKs from SEQ_MDL_LOOKUP_TYPE/SEQ_MDL_LOOKUP_VALUE, every FK resolved by natural key on KEY, bilingual NAME_AR/NAME_EN on every row, SORT_ORDER following srs-fin.md A6 listing order (which for the three status keys is also their A7 lifecycle order). A DO-block guard aborts the migration if SEC_MODULE_REG has no CODE='FIN' row (RULE-MDL-001 / XM-MDL-001 SOFT-READ; V24 supplies it). Per-key value counts: ACCOUNT_TYPE 5, DEBIT_CREDIT 2, PERIOD_STATE 4, FISCAL_YEAR_STATUS 2, JOURNAL_TYPE 5, JOURNAL_STATUS 3, ACCOUNT_DERIVATION_TYPE 3, AMOUNT_SOURCE_TYPE 3, DISTRIBUTION_TYPE 3, RECURRING_SCHEDULE_TYPE 2, RECURRING_FREQUENCY 4 — identical in srs-fin.md A6, P0/module-registry-fin.md LOOKUPS OWNED and P1/registry-srs-fin.md's count column, with no disagreement between the three. NOT FULLY GROUNDED — two keys seeded as TYPE ONLY, with ZERO values, because no artifact enumerates any: ACCOUNTING_EVENT_TYPE (A6: 'none seeded — host-specific, added as data [§3, §6.4]') and PAYMENT_METHOD (A6: 'none seeded — host-specific'; registry-srs-fin.md:42 adds 'registered, no dedicated column this v1'). Also not grounded by any artifact: the per-VALUE bilingual display labels (A6 lists codes only) — written as the standard Arabic/English accounting terms for each code, exactly as V20 did for NOTIF/FILE; TYPE-level labels are verbatim from module-registry-fin.md. api_doc_gaps.endpoint: PATCH /api/v1/fin/fiscal-periods/{id}/hard-close (API-FIN-026) and POST /api/v1/fin/fiscal-years/{id}/year-end-close (API-FIN-027) — the documented repair path for PERM_FIN_PERIODS_CLOSE_APPROVE does not work
api_doc_gaps.detail: V25's header (lines 56-61) prescribes the repair for the deliberately-ungranted close-approval permission: a human creates a close-approver role through SEC's live role administration and assigns it to a user who does not hold PERM_FIN_JOURNAL_ENTRIES_CREATE. That repair CANNOT succeed. JwtAuthenticationFilter.passesGateway (src/main/java/com/erp/sec/security/JwtAuthenticationFilter.java:132-141) splits a permission code at lastIndexOf('_') and requires the sibling <prefix>_VIEW to be held. For PERM_FIN_PERIODS_CLOSE_APPROVE the last underscore precedes APPROVE, so the filter demands PERM_FIN_PERIODS_CLOSE_VIEW — a code that exists in no registry row, no constant and no migration. toAuthorities (:121-128) therefore strips the authority even after a valid grant, and both endpoints answer 403 permanently. This is the ONLY FIN permission with a two-token action; every other multi-word FIN code splits correctly because the extra words sit in the screen segment. V24:39-43 and V25:64-67 both assert the gateway convention holds on every screen; for FIN_PERIODS/CLOSE_APPROVE it does not.
api_doc_gaps.resolution: HUMAN DECISION RECORDED (final) — RESOLVED by V27__fin_close_approver_role.sql. The SEC gateway defect this entry described is fixed independently: JwtAuthenticationFilter no longer splits a permission code at lastIndexOf('_'); MenuService.effectiveAuthorityCodes() now applies RULE-SEC-007 against the registry's own screen rows (RoleActionGrantDomain.isGatewayAction), so PERM_FIN_PERIODS_CLOSE_APPROVE survives authority resolution as long as the SAME screen also carries a granted VIEW row. A grant therefore now takes effect. Decision on the missing grant owner: rather than granting close-approval to SYS_ADMIN (which holds PERM_FIN_JOURNAL_ENTRIES_CREATE and would make the close permanently impossible), V27 mints a DEDICATED role FIN_CLOSE_APPROVER ('معتمد إقفال الفترات المالية' / 'Fiscal Period Close Approver'), code shape following the seeded <SCOPE>_<FUNCTION> convention (SYS_ADMIN, CU_ADMIN, FILE_ADMIN, NOTIF_ADMIN). It holds exactly: Tier-1 module FIN, Tier-2 screen FIN_PERIODS only, Tier-3 two action rows — PERM_FIN_PERIODS_VIEW (the gateway row V24 registered for this purpose) and PERM_FIN_PERIODS_CLOSE_APPROVE. It deliberately holds NOTHING else: not PERM_FIN_JOURNAL_ENTRIES_CREATE, not FIN_PERIODS CREATE/UPDATE, no other FIN screen. RULE-FIN-015 is thus satisfied by construction — the role cannot be assigned in a way that also confers entry creation through it. TWO OPERATIONAL PRECONDITIONS remain, documented in V27's header and NOT resolvable by migration: (1) V27 assigns the role to NO USER, and FinSeparationOfDutiesService.resolveFacts() reports closeApprovePermissionHeld = !approvers.isEmpty() while FiscalPeriodDomain.assertCanHardClose throws FIN-403-SOD-VIOLATION when that is false — so 'nobody holds close-approval' fails the close exactly as 'one user holds both' does; a real SEC_USER_ROLE assignment is still required before API-FIN-026/API-FIN-027 work. (2) The assignee MUST be a user holding no role that carries PERM_FIN_JOURNAL_ENTRIES_CREATE. The bootstrap 'admin' user holds SYS_ADMIN, which V25 granted that permission; since resolveFacts() compares the two user sets across each user's ROLE UNION, assigning FIN_CLOSE_APPROVER to 'admin' would put 'admin' in both sets and trip FIN-403-SOD-VIOLATION on every hard-close and year-end close. 'admin' is therefore deliberately NOT assigned. Verified against the live erp_db schema inside BEGIN/ROLLBACK: 1 role row, 1 module grant, 1 screen grant, 2 action grants, 0 user assignments; users holding PERM_FIN_PERIODS_CLOSE_APPROVE = {} and users holding PERM_FIN_JOURNAL_ENTRIES_CREATE = {admin} — disjoint.

api_doc_gaps.endpoint: POST /api/v1/fin/journal-entries/from-event (API-FIN-020) — RULE-FIN-010 remainder computation, and RULE-FIN-003's guard keying off a different column than the builder
api_doc_gaps.detail: Two related defects in remainder/percentage distribution (ACCOUNTING §12 point 6). (1) SIDE-BLIND REMAINDER: EventEntryService:135-153 accumulates every non-remainder line's amount into one flat 'assigned' total regardless of directionCode, then EventTypeRuleDomain.remainderAmount (:220-224) computes baseAmount - assigned. With base 1000 and lines DEBIT/FIELD=1000, CREDIT/PERCENTAGE 60%=600, CREDIT/REMAINDER, assigned = 1600 and the remainder computes to -600. The negative amount then trips CHK_FIN_JOURNAL_LINE_AMOUNT_POSITIVE (V22:425) and surfaces as an unlocalized 409 DATA_INTEGRITY_VIOLATION from GlobalExceptionHandler:79-87, not FIN-409-UNBALANCED. The remainder must be computed per side (debit total so far vs credit total so far). (2) GUARD/BUILDER COLUMN MISMATCH: EventTypeRuleDomain.assertRemainderLineSetValid (:109-126) only fires when some sibling line has distributionTypeCode = PERCENTAGE, and counts isRemainderFl; EventEntryService:137-143 decides remainder-ness from amountSourceTypeCode = REMAINDER. Two lines with amountSourceTypeCode = REMAINDER and distributionTypeCode = FIXED pass RuleLineService:76 unchallenged; at run time the first absorbs the whole residue and the second computes to 0, again dying on the DB CHECK. AllocationRuleDomain.assertRemainderTargetSetValid (:89-91, isRemainderFl) vs AllocationRuleService:222-227 (distributionTypeCode = REMAINDER) has the identical split. Rounding itself is correct where one remainder line exists: percentages use divide(100, scale 4, HALF_UP) and the remainder is an exact subtraction, so the residue is absorbed.
api_doc_gaps.resolution: RESOLVED — implemented in code and propagated to the specs. (1) PER-SIDE REMAINDER: EventTypeRuleDomain.remainderAmount now takes (opposingSideTotal, ownSideTotalSoFar) and EventEntryService.buildLines accumulates through the new JournalEntryDomain.SideTotals record, so the remainder is the difference between the two posting sides, never between a base amount and every line regardless of direction. Worked case from the detail (base 1000; DEBIT/FIELD 1000, CREDIT/PERCENTAGE 60% = 600.0000, CREDIT/REMAINDER): old −600.0000 → DB CHECK violation; new 400.0000 and the entry balances D1000 = C600+400. AC-FIN-012 (100 as 33%+33%+remainder against a DEBIT 100) now yields the AC's own 34.0000, where the side-blind form yielded −66.0000. A non-positive residue is no longer an opaque DATA_INTEGRITY_VIOLATION but the new FIN-422-REMAINDER-NOT-POSITIVE. The allocation path is unchanged arithmetically — its two arguments already WERE the opposing side's total (the source line) and its own side's running total. (2) SINGLE MARKER: isRemainderFl (DBF-FIN-103/141) is now the only marker. EventTypeRuleDomain.isRemainderLine / AllocationRuleDomain.isRemainderTarget are read by both builders; sourcedAmount and targetAmount return a plain BigDecimal and refuse a REMAINDER-typed line (FIN-422-REMAINDER-MARKER); and the RULE-FIN-003 guards now (a) reject any disagreement between isRemainderFl and the line's/target's own REMAINDER type code and (b) fire on 'any percentage sibling OR any line already marked remainder', so the two FIXED/REMAINDER lines of the detail are rejected at configuration time with FIN-409-REMAINDER-COUNT instead of dying on CHK_FIN_JOURNAL_LINE_AMOUNT_POSITIVE at run time. Specs: srs-fin.md §A5 RULE-FIN-003 and RULE-FIN-010 statements amended (the only two SRS rule edits made); Error Catalog + RULE→code coverage (both copies); API-FIN-011/016/017/020 Validations, Errors and Orchestration; DATA-DOM ENT-FIN-010/014. NOTE FOR OPERATIONS: any already-stored rule line or allocation target whose isRemainderFl disagrees with its type code now fails loudly at run time with FIN-422-REMAINDER-MARKER instead of silently mis-distributing — deliberate, and the ledger-safe direction of failure.

api_doc_gaps.endpoint: POST /api/v1/fin/journal-entries (API-FIN-019) — no coherence check between fiscalYearId, periodId and docDate
api_doc_gaps.detail: JournalEntryService.createManual (:159-180) resolves the fiscal year and the period by id INDEPENDENTLY and never checks that the period belongs to that year, nor that docDate falls within the period's start/end dates (DBF-FIN-080/081, both NOT NULL and available). Only checkTargetPeriodOpen runs. A caller may therefore post an entry stamped fiscalYearId = FY2025, periodId = an open period of FY2024, docDate = 2019-01-01. That row then appears in the FY2025 trial balance when scoped by periodId (aggregateAccountBalances filters period OR year, independently), is invisible to the balance sheet's asOfDate cut-off, and corrupts FiscalYearService.balancesOf (:270-272, scoped purely by journalEntry.fiscalYear) — that is, the year-end closing and opening entries themselves. The docNo counter is also scoped by the submitted year (:365-374), so the entry consumes a number in the wrong year's series. api_doc_gaps.detail: Three smaller defects in the year-end close body, all below the 403 that currently blocks the endpoint entirely. api_doc_gaps.resolution: RESOLVED for (a) and (b); (c) still needs the one-line human call. (a) ORDERING: FiscalYearService.yearEndClose now runs the SoD read (RULE-FIN-015, 403) first, then the year's own re-run guard, then the all-periods-Hard-Closed check (409), and only then resolves successorOf(...) and retainedEarningsAccount(). A deployment missing the successor year or the Retained Earnings marker therefore answers 403/409 as the javadoc and the plan both promise, instead of FIN-404-YEAR / FIN-404-ACCOUNT — test assertions on this endpoint are now writable either way. (b) RERUN GUARD: a new FiscalYearDomain (the entity's only Domain object; A.0.1 is unconditional and the guard's single fact is FiscalYear.statusCode, so DATA-DOM-MASTER's 'none scoped alone' no longer holds — its block is amended accordingly) carries assertCanYearEndClose(), which rejects a run against an already-CLOSED year with the catalog's EXISTING FIN-409-INVALID-TRANSITION row rather than a new code; it sits before the period check so a re-run is told the year is closed instead of the misleading FIN-409-PERIODS-NOT-CLOSED the first run's own YEAR_END_CLOSE transitions would raise. (c) EMPTY CLOSING ENTRY: left exactly as delivered and NOT guessed. REQ-FIN-036 and AC-FIN-036 require 'a balanced closing entry and a balanced opening entry', and POL-FIN-010 only requires result accounts to stand at zero afterwards — which a year with no result movement already satisfies. Nothing in P0/P1/P2/P3_1 chooses between posting a zero-line entry (today's behaviour, consuming a docNo), posting nothing (which breaks API-FIN-027's response contract, since it declares both entries) and refusing the close (which would block a legitimate dormant year). QUESTION FOR A HUMAN: when a fiscal year closes with no result account carrying a non-zero balance — and, symmetrically, no balance-sheet account carrying one — should API-FIN-027 post the zero-line entry, omit that entry from the response, or refuse the close? === UPDATE 2026-09-12 (governance-state alignment session) — part (c) is now RESOLVED; (a) and (b) stand as recorded above. DECISION: KEEP TODAY'S BEHAVIOUR — a dormant year-end close POSTS the zero-line CLOSING (and OPENING) entry, consuming a docNo. It was reviewed deliberately and kept, not left by default. Reasons, each checked against the code and the artifacts rather than asserted: posting it satisfies AC-FIN-036 LITERALLY, because JournalEntryDomain.checkBalanced sums debits and credits and returns empty when they compare equal, so 0 = 0 passes and a lineless entry is genuinely 'individually balanced'; OMITTING the entry would make AC-FIN-036's 'posts a closing entry' false and would also break API-FIN-027's declared response shape, which carries both entries; and REFUSING the close would invent a rule no artifact states, blocking a legitimate dormant year. NO CODE CHANGED — this is a decision recorded against behaviour that already shipped. It is now documented in the artifact rather than only here: see the DORMANT YEAR block at governance/modules/FIN/packages/backend-execution/SVC-API/SVC-API-INT.md:195-210, inside the <!-- API:API-FIN-027 --> block, which states the mechanism (FiscalYearService.closingLines contributes no line when every result account nets to zero and the Retained Earnings absorbing line is added only for a non-zero resultTotal; openingLines symmetrically), the docNo consumption (JournalPostingService.buildValidateAndPost allocates from the locked fiscal-year series before validating and writes unconditionally), the decision and its three-way rationale, and the containment fact that this shape is reachable ONLY from the internal year-end path because JournalEntryCreateRequest.lines carries @NotEmpty, so API-FIN-019 rejects a lineless entry at the DTO boundary. The question posed above is closed; do not re-open it as an unanswered gap.
